jobs.description:
Job Posting: Environmental Scientist (Limited-Term)

Department of Parks & Recreation

JC-534918



Environmental Scientist (Limited-Term)
  
ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST

$4,418.00 - $9,321.00 per Month
  
New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.

**Final Filing Date:** **11/2/2026**

**Application Methods:**

Electronic (Using your CalCareer Account)

By Mail

Drop-off

Print Job

Save Job

### **Job Description and Duties**

**ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST (LIMITED-TERM) – ANGELES DISTRICT/ NATURAL RESOURCES/ MALIBU CREEK STATE PARK**

  

The Angeles District has an opening for an Environmental Scientist (LT). Under the direction of the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory), serves as the coordinator for the Angeles District Natural Resources Volunteer Program. The incumbent coordinates, organizes, and oversees volunteer projects focused on habitat restoration, invasive plant removal, and community stewardship. This position provides guidance to ensure ecological goals and safety standards are met, while also building partnerships with community groups, schools, and nonprofits. The position is responsible for volunteer program reporting and contributes to the success of SMMC-funded wildfire recovery initiatives.
  
  
This position is a 12-month Limited-Term position that may be extended and/or become permanent.

The incumbent exercises a high degree of initiative, judgment, and analytical skill in coordinating sensitive and high-priority assignments that require collaboration with internal divisions, the Natural Resources Agency, control agencies, and other stakeholders.
  
  
This position is designated as not telework eligible.

  

Training and Development Assignments may be considered.

  

This position requires a valid Class C driver’s license. You must answer the questions addressing your driver’s license on your application. Ensure you provide your driver’s license number, class, expiration date, and any endorsements and/or restrictions on your application.

The selected candidate is required to submit to a background investigation process utilizing Live Scan fingerprinting prior to appointment.

**State housing is not available.** For further information contact Jacoub Mahshi at (424) 508-0465 or Jacoub.Mahshi@parks.ca.gov.

**This recruitment may be used to fill identical vacancies which may occur within 180 days of the Final Filing Date of this job posting.**

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

### **Working Conditions**

Effective July 1, 2025, the California Department of Human Resources (CalHR) implemented the Personal Leave Program 2025 (PLP 2025). PLP 2025 directs that each employee receives a temporary reduction in pay in exchange for PLP 2025 leave credits. The percentage of the temporary salary reduction and the number of PLP 2025 leave credits are determined by the position’s assigned bargaining unit. **The salary range(s) included in this job advertisement do not reflect the temporary salary reduction.** For additional information regarding PLP 2025, please click here.  
  
  
  
  
Work environment is an office/outdoor setting, using computers, telephone and other business equipment. Typical work activities involve frequent and prolonged periods of sitting. Typical work involves extended telephone conversations and keyboard operation. Must meet many deadlines within short time frames. Hand dexterity to use telephone, keyboard and calculators are common requirements. Move about, stand, reach, stoop or bend. Use fine motor skills for computer or office machine use. Lift minimum weight of 25 pounds. Use of hand cart to move supplies over 10 pounds of weight. Requires reaching, twisting, turning, kneeling, bending, stooping, squatting, crouching, grasping and making repetitive hand movements in the performance of daily duties. May involve some exposure to aggressive visitors. Will work outdoors in unpredictable weather ranging from extreme heat to extreme cold. May be required to perform arduous field work in rugged, steep terrain. May encounter wild animals. Must be willing to work weekends, nights, and holidays as necessary. Travel maybe required to meetings, conferences, trainings, and on site project locations and may need to use personal vehicle if State Vehicles are not available.

### **Department Information**

The mission of California State Parks is to provide for the health, inspiration, and education of the people of California by helping to preserve the state's extraordinary biological diversity, protecting its most valued natural and cultural resources, and creating opportunities for high-quality outdoor recreation.

All employees are responsible for contributing to an inclusive, safe, and secure work environment that values diverse cultures, perspectives, and experiences, and is free from discrimination.

Department Website: http://www.parks.ca.gov

jobs.description:
**Salary: $220,000 - $250,000 / year**

**Other Forms of Compensation:** Annual bonus potential

**Pay Grade:** 19

**A family of companies and experiences**

As the leading foodservice and support services company, Compass Group USA is known for our great people, great service and our great results. If you’ve been hungry and away from home, chances are you’ve tasted Compass Group’s delicious food and experienced our outstanding service. We have over 284,000 US associates who work in award-winning restaurants, corporate cafes, hospitals, schools, arenas, museums, and more in all 50 states. Our reach is constantly expanding to shape the industry and create new opportunities for innovation. Join the Compass family today!

**great people. great services. great results.**

Each and every individual plays a key role in the growth and legacy of our company. We know the next big idea can come from anyone. We encourage developing and attracting expertise that differentiates us as a company as we continue to raise the bar.

**Job Summary:**
----------------

**The Vice President, Environmental Health, Safety & Operational Risk** provides strategic and operational leadership for environmental health, safety, quality, and risk management across Support Services, with a primary focus on the rapidly growing Data Centers business.

The role operates across Support Services environments that may include data centers, mission-critical and critical environments, facilities management and integrated facilities management, advanced manufacturing, semiconductor and cleanroom operations, life sciences, healthcare facilities, construction, commissioning, capital projects, industrial operations, infrastructure, utilities, and other 24/7 hard-services and engineering operations.

This leader establishes enterprise standards, programs, and performance objectives that protect employees, contractors, clients, and customers while enabling safe growth, operational reliability, and consistent execution. The VP serves as a senior advisor to Support Services leadership and partners with Operations, Engineering, Construction, Facilities, Human Resources, Procurement, Legal, and client leadership.

***This is a remote role and may be based near any major airport in the U.S.***

**Key Responsibilities:**

**EHS Strategy, Governance & Risk Management**

* Lead the EHS and operational risk strategy for Support Services, with particular emphasis on data centers, mission-critical facilities, critical environments, and complex technical operations.
* Establish scalable EHS policies, management systems, programs, and performance expectations that can be consistently applied across diverse operating environments and client requirements.
* Identify, assess, and mitigate current and emerging risks associated with new technologies, capital projects, client transitions, acquisitions, and evolving operating models.
* Ensure compliance with applicable safety, environmental, regulatory, client, and company requirements; serve as the senior resource for significant EHS and operational risk matters.
* Establish minimum contractor selection criteria based on safety performance, capabilities, regulatory history, staffing, training, and subcontractor controls.

**Operational Readiness, Construction & Commissioning**
-------------------------------------------------------

* Integrate EHS requirements into project development, construction, commissioning, mobilization, operational readiness, site launches, and ongoing 24/7 operations.
* Provide leadership for electrical safety, contractor safety, high-risk activities, emergency preparedness, life safety, incident management, and other risks associated with hard services and engineering operations.
* Establish governance for contractor and vendor qualification, onboarding, performance management, audits, corrective action, and continuous improvement.

**Performance, Assurance & Continuous Improvement**

* Establish meaningful EHS KPIs, dashboards, reporting, and assurance processes to identify trends, measure performance, manage risk, and drive continuous improvement.
* Provide oversight of incident investigations, crisis response, root-cause analysis, and corrective and preventive actions; ensure lessons learned are shared across Support Services.
* Partner with clients and senior leaders to establish shared EHS expectations and risk-management strategies for critical and complex operating environments.

**Growth, Leadership & Culture**

* Provide EHS leadership and due diligence for new business, strategic pursuits, client transitions, mobilizations, acquisitions, and other growth initiatives.
* Build and develop a high-performing EHS organization and strengthen safety leadership capability throughout the business.
* Promote a culture in which safety, risk management, quality, and operational excellence are integrated into business decisions rather than managed as separate compliance activities.
* Provide oversight, where applicable, of specialized safety and quality programs, including food safety, HACCP, preventive controls, GMPs, supplier quality, and related regulatory requirements.

**Required Qualifications:**
----------------------------

* Bachelor's degree in Safety, Environmental Health, Engineering, Quality, or a related field preferred.
* 12+ years of progressive EHS, environmental, safety, risk, quality, or operational leadership experience.
* Demonstrated experience leading multi-site or enterprise EHS programs and developing high-performing teams.
* Experience in complex, regulated, high-risk, mission-critical, construction, manufacturing, healthcare, infrastructure, utilities, or comparable operating environments.
* Strong knowledge of OSHA and applicable environmental, safety, and regulatory requirements.
* Demonstrated experience with contractor risk management, incident management, audits, corrective action, risk assessment, and EHS management systems.
* Strong executive
